title: PAT permission error on pre-merge checklist — 'Resource not accessible by personal access token'
description: The PP review page shows a red error 'Resource not accessible by personal access token' in the pre-merge checklist. The GitHub PAT used by the app to check branch protection / merge status doesn't have sufficient permissions for the target repo (permission-protocol/app). Likely needs contents:read or pull_requests:read scope on the fine-grained PAT. Repo: permission-protocol/app, pre-merge checklist API calls.

title: Pre-merge checklist stuck on 'Checking' — branch/conflict status never resolves
description: After PP approval and all GitHub checks passing (6/6 green), the PP review page pre-merge checklist still shows 'Checking' for 'Branch up to date' and 'No conflicts'. The Merge & Deploy button stays disabled even though GitHub shows the PR is mergeable. The checklist polling/refresh logic doesn't pick up the final GitHub mergeable state. Repo: permission-protocol/app, review page component.

title: GitHub Action marketplace README overhaul — screenshot, 30-second setup, copy-paste workflow
description: The deploy-gate Action is the top-of-funnel for every developer who finds PP. The marketplace README needs: a hero screenshot of the gate blocking + approval flow, a 30-second quickstart (3 steps: install action, set API key, push), and a complete copy-paste workflow YAML. Most GitHub Actions get adopted from README alone — no one reads docs. Files: action.yml description + README.md in the deploy-gate action repo.

title: Rich gate-failure CI output — file summary, risk badge, and direct approve URL
description: When deploy-gate blocks a PR in CI, the GitHub Action output is the first thing Marco sees. Make it count: show a markdown summary of changed files grouped by risk tier (critical/standard/low), the AI-generated summary, and a clickable approve URL. This turns the 'failure' moment into a product touchpoint. Modify the deploy-gate action's failure output template in the GitHub Action source (action.yml + the verify endpoint response).

title: Inline diff viewer on approval page — see code changes without leaving PP
description: Sarah shouldn't have to context-switch to GitHub to see what changed. Embed a syntax-highlighted diff viewer directly on the approval page, pulling file diffs from the GitHub API. Collapsible per-file, with the blast radius risk badge next to each file. The approval page becomes self-contained — everything needed to make the decision is right there. Files: new diff-viewer component + GitHub diff API integration in the deploy request detail page.

title: Distinct Production Environment Alert
description: Enhance the approval screen (e.g., `src/app/approvals/[id]/page.tsx`) with a highly visible visual alert for 'production' environment deployments. This could be a prominent amber banner across the top of the screen or a distinct border, aligning with the 'Environment theming' decision. The environment information would be retrieved from the approval request data (e.g., `src/app/api/approvals/[id]/route.ts`) and used to conditionally render a new `EnvironmentBanner` component.

title: One-click approve via direct URL — no dashboard navigation needed
description: Marco wants to approve in under 5 seconds. Create a direct approval endpoint: /approve/[requestId]?token=[one-time-token] that shows a minimal approval card (repo, PR#, summary, risk badge) with a single Approve button. No login required if token is valid. Generate this URL when the deploy request is created, include it in the gate failure output and PR comment. This removes the 'go find it on the dashboard' step entirely. Files: new route at src/app/approve/[requestId]/page.tsx + token generation in the verify route.

title: Clearly label AI agent source on approval screen
description: Enhance the approval screen's 'Context' zone (e.g., in `app/components/approval-screen/context-zone.tsx`) to prominently display if the PR originated from an AI agent like Codex or Claude. This involves parsing the PR description or author to identify known AI agents and rendering a specific label or icon.

title: Post-Install AI Agent Config Guide
description: After a user installs the GitHub App, if no AI agent-specific configuration is found in their `.github/workflows/deploy-gate.yml`, display a guided prompt on the `app/page.tsx` dashboard. This prompt, potentially using a new `app/components/ai-config-onboarding.tsx` component, would walk Marco through adding common AI bot IDs or commit patterns to the action to ensure proper detection and gating.

title: AI-Generated Summary of Code Changes
description: Integrate an LLM to generate a 2-3 sentence summary of the proposed code changes for AI agent-generated PRs. This summary would appear in the 'Context' or 'Assessment' zone of the approval screen (e.g., `src/app/approvals/[id]/page.tsx`). It would call a new or existing LLM API endpoint (e.g., `src/app/api/llm/summarize-diff`) with the diff, and display the result in a dedicated UI element, helping users quickly grasp the PR's intent.

title: Policy Adherence Summary on Approval Screen
description: In the 'Assessment' zone of the approval screen (e.g., `src/app/approvals/[id]/page.tsx`), add a section showing a concise summary of how the AI agent's proposed changes align with configured rulesets. For instance, display 'Security Policy: ✅ Passed' or 'Critical Files Modified: ❌ Failed'. This would query `src/app/api/approvals/[id]/route.ts` for ruleset evaluation results and render them in a new component within the approval flow.

title: Blast radius indicator on approval page — file risk categorization
description: Sarah needs to know what she's approving at a glance. Add a blast radius section to the approval detail page that categorizes changed files into risk tiers: critical (migrations, auth, deploy configs, env vars), standard (business logic, API routes), and low (tests, docs, styles). Pull the file list from the GitHub PR diff API. Show a simple red/yellow/green badge. Files: src/app/pp/deploy-requests/[requestId]/page.tsx + new blast-radius utility.

title: Approval Screen Diff Highlight for AI Changes
description: On the approval detail screen, when displaying file changes, visually distinguish lines or files that were exclusively modified by an AI agent. This could involve adding a subtle background tint or a small AI icon next to affected lines within the `app/components/diff-viewer/inline-diff.tsx` component, helping Sarah quickly focus her review on agent-generated code.

title: 30-second onboarding wizard — GitHub App install → first gate in 3 clicks
description: New users hit a wall between 'this sounds cool' and 'it works on my repo.' Build a guided onboarding flow: (1) Install GitHub App, (2) Select repo, (3) Copy workflow YAML — done. Auto-detect if the action is already installed and show the first pending request. Remove every friction point between signup and first gate. Files: new onboarding route (src/app/setup/page.tsx) + GitHub App installation callback handler.

title: Prisma FK violation on supersededByRequestId during deploy request creation
description: When the deploy-gate action calls the verify endpoint to create a new deploy request, the supersede logic fails with Foreign key constraint violated: DeployGateRequest_supersededByRequestId_fkey. This prevents request creation entirely, which means REQUEST_ID is empty in the CI output. Root cause: the supersede logic tries to link to a request ID that doesn't exist or was already deleted. Repo: permission-protocol/app, file: src/app/api/v1/receipts/verify/route.ts (supersede logic around request creation).

title: GitHub App not installed error should guide user to install — actionable CTA instead of dead-end banner
description: When the PP review page detects the GitHub App isn't installed on the target repo, it shows a red banner 'GitHub App not installed on this repo (owner/repo)' — but gives no guidance on how to fix it. This should be an actionable card with: (1) a direct 'Install GitHub App' button linking to the App's installation page with the repo pre-selected, (2) brief explanation of why it's needed ('PP needs the GitHub App to check branch status and merge PRs'), (3) a 'Refresh' button to re-check after installation. This is the #1 onboarding friction point — users who get here after approving will bounce if they can't merge. Repo: permission-protocol/app, review page pre-merge checklist component.

title: AI "Should I worry?" verdict on deploy requests
description: Add a single-line AI verdict at the top of the PP review page that classifies the deploy request as 🟢 Routine, 🟡 Review carefully, or 🔴 High risk. The enrichment pipeline (src/lib/enrichment/enrich.ts) already computes riskLevel and AI summary. This feature distills that into one actionable signal. For 🟢: "UI component added, no API/auth/data changes". For 🟡: "Touches authentication flow" or "Modifies API routes". For 🔴: "Changes payment logic" or "Modifies secrets handling". The verdict appears above the fold in the Context zone of the review page (src/app/pp/deploy-requests/[requestId]/page.tsx). Use the existing assessmentSummary.riskLevel + diff file categorization from categorizeFileRisk() to generate the verdict text. No new API calls needed — all data is already in the enrichment response.

title: Visual preview screenshots in PP review page
description: Embed before/after screenshots of affected pages in the PP deploy request review page. When a PR has a Vercel preview deployment, capture screenshots of key pages (the ones changed in the PR) and display them side-by-side in the review page. Implementation: (1) Add a Vercel preview URL field to DeployGateRequest model or extract from GitHub deployment status API. (2) Use a serverless screenshot service (or Playwright/Puppeteer on the server) to capture the preview URL and the production URL for comparison. (3) Display in a new "Visual Preview" section in the review page (src/app/pp/deploy-requests/[requestId]/page.tsx) between the AI summary and the action buttons. (4) For the factory pipeline: the PRD already lists affected pages — pass those as screenshot targets. Start with a simple approach: just screenshot the preview URL root and show it. No diffing needed initially — humans are great at visual comparison.

title: [permission-protocol/cli] Framework detector — identify agent frameworks in codebase
description:
GitHub Issue: https://github.com/permission-protocol/cli/issues/2

## Goal
Detect which AI agent frameworks are used in a scanned project. This feeds into the permission gap analyzer (issue #3).

## Supported Frameworks (v1)
Detect via package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, go.mod, pom.xml, and import statements:

| Framework | Package/Import | Language |
|-----------|---------------|----------|
| LangChain | `langchain`, `@langchain/*` | Python, TS |
| LangGraph | `langgraph`, `@langchain/langgraph` | Python, TS |
| CrewAI | `crewai` | Python |
| Open
